articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA—the agency supposed to keep us cyber-secure—casually left AWS credentials on public GitHub like it's 2010. At least they're consistent with government security standards: nonexistent.

articles.title: 'Claw Chain' Vulnerabilities Threaten OpenClaw Deployments
articles.summary: Microsoft Exchange is getting owned via XSS and there's no patch yet. Classic Microsoft move—ship broken, patch never.

articles.title: We Updated Our Privacy Policy. Here's What Changed and Why.
articles.summary: Meta's internal docs reveal they planned to launch facial recognition for smart glasses during political chaos to avoid criticism. Because nothing says 'ethical tech' like surveillance timing.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: EFF drops a guide on fighting digital surveillance abuses across the Americas. Because apparently we need instructions on why mass spying is bad.

articles.title: Trapdoor Android Ad Fraud Scheme Hit 659 Million Daily Bid Requests Using 455 Apps
articles.summary: Linux kernel flaw lets unprivileged users peek at root-only files, because even Torvalds' baby isn't immune to privilege escalation shenanigans. ModuleJail might fix this mess.

articles.title: The New Phishing Click: How OAuth Consent Bypasses MFA
articles.summary: DirtyDecrypt PoC dropped for Linux kernel CVE-2026-31635 local privilege escalation. Because if you're going to own a box, might as well do it with style.

articles.title: Anthropic Will Update Regulators on Mythos’ Cyber Vulnerability Findings
articles.summary: Hackers demanded ransom from Grafana Labs to not release their already-open-source code. Galaxy brain criminal logic right there—extorting someone for public data.

articles.title: Your 401(k) is the new identity theft target
articles.summary: ShinyHunters hit 7-Eleven for 600k+ Salesforce records and demanded ransom. Nothing says 'Big Gulp' like a data breach with your Slurpee.

articles.title: Grafana Labs refuses ransom after hackers steal already-open-source code
articles.summary: SEPPMail Secure E-Mail Gateway has critical RCE vulns that let attackers read arbitrary emails. Secure email gateway that's not secure—peak enterprise software right there.

articles.title: Linux kernel flaw opens root-only files to unprivileged users
articles.summary: Shai-Hulud copycat worm infects npm packages because JavaScript developers never learn. The spice must flow, but maybe not through your package manager.
